name: Screen, window and tab capture
plain: Asks to record or stream a screen, window or browser tab.
meaning: Gives the site a live copy of whatever the person picks: their whole screen, an app window, or a tab. Can expose private messages, tabs and credentials visible on screen.

web.api: navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({video, audio, preferCurrentTab, selfBrowserSurface, systemAudio, surfaceSwitching, monitorTypeSurfaces, controller})

access.prompt_ui: Browser-drawn chooser every time: Chrome tab, window, entire screen tabs; Share audio checkbox; Firefox and Safari simple list. No stored grant: each call prompts. Indicator bar Stop sharing stays visible while active.
access.persistence: None: every call needs a fresh gesture and picker choice
access.revocation: Stop sharing button, closing the shared surface, or track.stop()
steps: Call getDisplayMedia from a click handler
Person picks tab, window or screen and optionally audio
Promise resolves with MediaStream; constraints apply only to the picked surface

data.metric: Video (and optional audio) of the chosen surface
data.update: continuous, frame rate up to about 30 fps default

fields.name: displaySurface
fields.precision: hint only; reflects what was picked

limits.headline: Can see the screen, window or tab you choose to share, until you stop
limits.user_action: You click Share screen or Present, then pick a tab, window or screen in the browser chooser
can: Show a live copy of the tab, window or whole screen you pick
Send that view to others on a call or into a recording
Include the sound of a shared tab if you tick the audio box
Record the shared view in the page
cannot: Start sharing without the browser chooser, which appears every time
See anything you did not pick in the chooser
Remember your choice, so the next share asks again
Work on iPhone or Android browsers, which do not offer screen sharing to sites
limits.differs: Desktop browsers only. Chrome can share tab audio; Firefox and Safari show a simpler list. Phone browsers do not support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a website record or live stream your screen, a window or a browser tab.

marketing.name: getDisplayMedia
marketing.pitch: Developer docs say a page can capture a screen, window or tab after the person picks what to share.

story.for_you: A browser picker opens and you choose what to share: your whole screen, one window, or one tab. A banner or border shows while sharing is on, and you can stop with one click.
story.for_makers: Screen sharing is what makes web calls, demos, support and game streaming work with no download. It also lets a maker record bug reports or train and test tools using what the user sees. The picker means the maker cannot grab more than the person chose.

use_cases.example: In a browser video call you click Share screen, pick a window, and your coworkers see your spreadsheet.
A cloud gaming site streams a game to your tab, and a streaming tool captures a game window so you can go live on Twitch from the browser.
A screen recorder in Chrome captures your tab and your voice to produce a how to video, saved right to your computer.
A support agent asks you to share your screen, so they can see an error message and walk you through the fix.
A coding class student shares an editor tab so the teacher can see their code in real time.
A bug report tool records your tab for 30 seconds and attaches the clip to a ticket for the engineers.
A scam site tricks you into sharing a fake support window, then watches your screen for bank details, which is why the picker matters.

risks: Private messages or passwords visible on shared screen
Tricking people into sharing the wrong window

technical_bounds: Site cannot silently capture: picker every call
Cannot choose the surface for the person
Audio only for tabs on most platforms, system audio on Windows and ChromeOS

abuse: Social engineering to share a banking tab
